key_insight: Using the entrywise maximum matrix norm yields an exact mixed-integer quadratic reformulation of Wasserstein distributionally robust chance-constrained standard quadratic optimization.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports risk-aware quadratic decisions over simplex weights, with applications such as portfolio allocation and machine learning under distributional uncertainty.
method: Model distributional uncertainty with a Wasserstein ball around the empirical distribution of sampled matrices.
Exploit linear dependence on the uncertain matrix to obtain an exact mixed-integer quadratic reformulation under the entrywise maximum norm.
Interpret the objective as worst-case Value-at-Risk and identify settings that reduce to one deterministic instance.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments on positive-definite and indefinite instances examine how model parameters affect optimal values and solution times, highlighting the computational cost of indefiniteness.
watch_item: An exact reformulation does not remove the underlying nonconvex difficulty; indefinite instances can remain computationally costly.
paper_title: Distributionally robust chance-constrained standard quadratic optimization with Wasserstein ambiguity
